Each is a blunder: pos1 dxe8=R+ misses forced #+4, pos8 Bxc7 abandons the b2 rook (Rxb2+), pos9 Rxe8 allows #+2. No single hanging piece dominates (major-piece class ~80%); trajectory is "mixed" (0.11) and best move is "quiet" only 51%.
verdicts.reason: Chip correctly captures "capture + blunder" (98% captures, evals confirm blunders) but misstates the key element: the data's "hanging" is the player's OWN piece left en prise AFTER the move (hang_after in pos 1,3,4,5,7,8,9,10), not a free piece the player grabbed — the summaries show captures that abandon defense or miss mate, not greedy grabs; and "missed a stronger non-capture (often mate)" is only clear in pos 1 and 9 (best_type quiet just 0.51).
verdicts.fix: "Capture that leaves a piece hanging (blunder)" — a capture move that drops the player's own material en prise (queen or rook most often). Keep the piece generic (no single piece dominates) and frame the hang as the move's consequence, not a free piece captured.

verdicts.claims: Chip: "Knight captures leaving piece hanging" — played a knight capture (Nx_) that leaves a piece en prise; missed move is a non-capture that avoids hanging material.
verdicts.show: All 10 played moves are knight captures (Nxe5 x4, Nxd5 x4, Nxd4, Nxe4) and all 10 leave the capturing knight en prise by SEE — hang_after = "knight(loses 3)" in every single position (pos 1-10).
verdicts.reason: Both chip claims — knight capture and a piece left hanging — hold in 10/10 positions with no overclaim (no fork/square/victim named, and the 51% blunder_piece fact is moot since the top10 is 100% knight).

verdicts.claims: Blunders in the middlegame where the played move was a quiet (non-capture) move; the missed alternative was a stronger, often tactical move.
verdicts.show: All 10 are middlegame blunders the player made. 8/10 are non-captures; pos6 Bxb2 is an explicit capture (pawn-grab) and pos7 g4e5 is possibly a capture. Piece skew the chip wisely leaves un-named: 6/10 are knight moves (f3h4, c5d7, Nd2, f3e5, g4e5, g5h3), 2 bishop (Bc2, Bxb2), 1 rook (a1e1), 1 pawn (b5b4) — none above 60%, so no piece should be claimed. Material is mixed: 4/10 leave something en prise (pos1 pawn, pos2 knight(3), pos4 pawn, pos5 knight(3)), 6/10 hang nothing. The 3 cached evals confirm blunders of varying size (+655→#+7; +528→+694 ~166cp in a lost position; -19→+188 ~207cp).
verdicts.reason: Both named axes hold across the 10 positions — middlegame (9-10/10, fact 92%) and non-capture (8/10, fact 84%, with only Bxb2 a clear capture, within tolerance) — and "blunder" is given by the dataset; critically it does NOT overspecify a piece/tactic despite a 60% knight skew, so there is no over- or under-claim.

verdicts.claims: Chip: "Middlegame quiet move blunders" — a non-capture (quiet) move in the middlegame that is a mistake, missing a stronger continuation. No specific piece or tactic claimed.
verdicts.show: All 10 are non-capture middlegame moves (mostly rook lifts: Rc8, Re8, Rac1, Rd8, Rc1, Rh8, Rd1, plus Nd2). 8/10 are confirmable blunders: positions 2/6/7 hang a knight (−3), 1/4/8 hang a pawn (−1), and 3/4/10 have eval drops of 242/220/324cp. Positions 5 and 9 (hang none, eval cached as ?) are unverifiable.
verdicts.reason: Chip's three claims all hold across the set: middlegame (97%), quiet/non-capture (81%, all 10 positions), and blunder (8/10 confirmable via en-prise material or eval drop); it wisely avoids naming a piece despite rook being a 45% plurality, so no overspecification.

verdicts.claims: A middlegame blunder where the queen is moved to a suboptimal square without capturing; missed a stronger non-queen move or a queen capture.
verdicts.show: Only 4/10 are confirmed queen non-captures (Qd7, Qd4, Qf4, Qb6), and those do fit a 'queen to suboptimal square' theme. The other 6 are UCI moves, several clearly non-queen: f6f5 is a pawn push, g8f8 is a king/rook move that leaves a knight en prise (hang_after knight loses 3), f7g6 is a diagonal king/pawn move. 8/10 hang nothing (hang_after none); only Qd7 (pawn) and g8f8 (knight) leave material en prise, so this is not a hanging-piece feature. The genuine shared thread is middlegame, non-capture, eval-dropping moves.
verdicts.reason: The 'queen' claim is named as the rule but blunder_piece is only 0.70, and the top-10 contains clear non-queen counterexamples (f6f5 pawn push, g8f8 king/rook hanging a knight), while the actually-concentrated signals are non-capture (0.81) and middlegame (0.84).
verdicts.fix: Middlegame non-capture blunders, often (not always) misplacing the queen
